1000215.etyen:
The precise origin of the given name is uncertain. It may be a pet form of female given names ending in -enna, -enne, -enni or -enny, or a variant of Ena (“female given name”).
Another possibility is that Enna represents a Nordic adaptation of German Änne or Änni, pet forms of Anna. German Änne is a variant of Anna and Anne. Under this analysis, the name ultimately derives from Late Latin Anna (“female given name”), from Koine Greek Ἄννα (Ánna, “Anna”), from Biblical Hebrew חַנָּה (Ḥannāh, “Hannah; grace, favour”).
The name may alternatively derive from German short forms of compound names beg

1004567.etyen:
From Guri + -ine or Guro + -ine.
Guri continues Old Norse Guðríðr, while Guro continues Old Norse Guðrún. First attested in the 18th century in Norway.
Compare Swedish Gurine (“female given name”).
